programme.title: The Lost Neanderthals
programme.desc: The Mandrin Cave in southern France has been attracting the attention of archaeologists for 30 years. The cave was regularly occupied in prehistoric times, and a remarkable record of human habitation going back thousands of years has been preserved by its soils. In 2015, the remains of a Neanderthal were uncovered, and the archaeological evidence points to this individual, named Thorin, living in close proximity to newly arrived Homo sapiens. This documentary follows an international team of scientists as they discover and investigate precious relics of the Palaeolithic period, resulting in groundbreaking revelations about the human populations of around 50,000 years ago as researchers uncover some of the secrets of the Mandrin Cave.

programme.title: Yellowstone: Wildest Winter to Blazing Summer
programme.desc: Patrick follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Hungry wolves are struggling to bring down their elk prey in the unusually shallow snow. And for great grey owls, it is the iciness of the snow that is hampering their hunts. Yellowstone's winter is always one of the most brutal on the planet. But 2016 saw weather records broken, and the wildlife was forced to adapt to survive. Kate Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season, from understanding the importance of the snowpack's structure as the melt begins to uncovering why Yellowstone's unique geology poses problems for some grazers' teeth.

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed

programme.title: Blue Velvet

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: From the magical films of the silent era to the celebrated work of director David Lean and high definition television, this documentary revisits films and interviews from the archive to answer the question of why Dickens's novels have inspired so many hundreds of adaptations on screen. This co-production with Dickens 2012 not only encapsulates the history of Dickens's time, but also of the 100 years in which his work has survived most acutely on screen. It is not only the stories, themes and characters of Dickens's writing that translate so well onto screen - Sergei Eisenstein argued that there is something essentially filmic in his unique prose style; that Dickens's rapid 'cutting' within scenes and from scene to scene coupled with his seamless mixture of the bizarrely comic with the terrifyingly profound was itself proto-cinematic. Dickens wrote the way a camera saw before film had been invented, and he remains to this day the most cinematic of writers.

programme.title: The Crucible: 40 Golden Snooker Years
programme.desc: Steve Davis goes back to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield to celebrate 40 years of the World Snooker Championship. If the walls of this famous regional theatre could talk, they would tell tales of tears, triumphs, occasional debauchery, laughter and top-class sport. With contributions from snooker legends Dennis Taylor, Stephen Hendry, Jimmy White and super-fans Stephen Fry and Richard Osman.

programme.title: Davis v Taylor: The '85 Black Ball Final
programme.desc: A look back at one of British sport's golden moments - the 1985 World Championship Snooker final. At its peak, over 18 and a half million people sat glued to their sets as Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor battled past midnight to a final and deciding black ball, BBC Two's biggest ever audience. Colin Murray journeys around the UK filling in the gaps on the first time that he was allowed to see the other side of midnight. Along the way he finds answers to questions such as where did Dennis's 'upside-down glasses' actually come from? What really went on behind those dressing room doors? How did you spread the news in a world without mobile phones? And how different would the lives of the two protagonists have been if the result had been reversed that night? Featuring contributions from Barry McGuigan, Ted Lowe, Stephen Hendry and Barry Hearn.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Cambridgeshire, the East Anglian air ambulance races to save farmer Jonathan Willis after a freak accident leaves him impaled on his forklift. When the crew arrive, they realise one wrong move could prove fatal. The rescue is complex and high risk, with medics battling to stabilise Jonathan in the middle of his own yard, before rushing him to a specialist major trauma unit. Featuring dramatic CCTV footage of the incident and first-hand accounts from Jonathan, his wife Wendy and paramedic Andy Bates, this is an extraordinary story of split-second decisions and sheer determination in the fight to save a life. Meanwhile, in the Scottish Highlands, farmers face devastating attacks on their lambs by white-tailed eagles, threatening livelihoods and sparking debate over how to protect flocks. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan joins police tackling the surge in illegal fly-tipping, exposing how organised gangs are blighting farmland across the region.

The rivalry leads to plenty of friendly competition around the fair and dishes up some drama at the auction! Charlie Ross visits nearby Lullingstone Castle, former site of the UK’s first silk farm, and learns about some unusual former residents.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Amanda Holden is stepping into the fight against fraud – and this time, it’s personal. After scammers used her name and image to con victims out of thousands, Amanda is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Amanda joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those pretending to be her. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team will hack the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting the fraudsters and stopping scams before they happen.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives

programme.title: Escape to the Country

Alistair also meets a willow farmer and discovers how this wonderfully sustainable crop is being woven into the future.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading. In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late. Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in Clapham, a terrace in Kent and a bungalow in Stoke-on-Trent are all sold under the hammer. Jacqui, Martin and Dion meet the successful bidders, including a mother and daughter taking on their first family development and a part-time property developer who spends more than five times his original budget.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone. Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction. Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks?

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: 1983. A young surfer leaves Dolphin Cove in pursuit of his dreams. Forty-three years later, his remains are found in the concrete by the ocean pool. But how is that possible when he left town before the concrete was even poured? Mackenzie has her work cut out, with decades separating the investigation from the crime. The grim discovery stirs painful memories of Philomena's past, forcing her to confront history and heartache. Glenn's no stranger to that as he struggles to let go of his feelings for Mack, all while her connection with his replacement Leo blooms.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong hosts, with guest panellists actor and comedian Chris McCausland and journalist Cindy Yu joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: Bill’s exciting new life comes crashing down when he learns that his lodgers have given themselves nicknames but left him out. Hurt, Bill ramps up his eccentricities in the hope of providing the inspiration for a new moniker, only for his odd behaviour to confirm the students’ suspicion that they’re living with a weirdo.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: BBC London

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show
programme.desc: On Graham's sofa are Hollywood star and four-time Oscar nominee Willem Dafoe, talking about his new film Werwulf; Slow Horses star Jack Lowden, playing Mr Darcy in the new Netflix adaptation of Pride and Prejudice; Strictly judge Shirley Ballas, embarking on the Strictly Come Dancing live tour; and comedian and actor Jack Whitehall, talking about his upcoming arena tour, Bad Influence. Plus music from singer-songwriter Sienna Spiro, performing Pure.

programme.title: The Preacher's Wife
programme.desc: The good-natured Reverend Henry Biggs finds that his marriage to choir mistress Julia is flagging due to his constant absence caring for the deprived. The Rev Biggs prays to God for help - and help arrives in the form of an angel named Dudley.

programme.title: Weather for the Week Ahead
programme.desc: Detailed weather forecast.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Ben Lippett and Paul Ainsworth, and by special guest Jack Dee. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: As Nigella says, 'Part of the balance of life lies in understanding that different days require different types of eating'. So in this episode, Nigella shares her favourite menu to help get that balance in the kitchen. For the days when something light and luscious is needed, Nigella's salad of salmon, avocado, watercress and pumpkin seeds fits perfectly. For the occasions that call for something a bit different, there is Nigella's chicken shawarma with an array of spices, sauces and flatbreads. Inspired by a spit-roasted Lebanese kebab, Nigella's oven-roasted version is fun, tasty and prefect for feeding a crowd. There has to be chocolate in the balance and Nigella shares two of her latest treats - a glossy liquorice and blackcurrant chocolate cake and her chocolate chip cookie dough pots - freshly baked pots of gooey cookie dough served with a dollop of ice cream or creme fraiche.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross is in Shropshire, where experts Tim Weeks and Ben Cooper try to help the teams make big profits when they head to the auction in Malvern. Charlie takes a trip into Shrewsbury to learn about the history of some 15th-century merchants, the Shrewsbury Drapers, and how they made the town so prosperous.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Snooker: UK Championship
programme.desc: Live coverage from day 1 of the 2026 UK Snooker Championship.

programme.title: Final Score
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest news, analysis, reaction and interviews from the afternoon’s biggest football matches.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: BBC London
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather from London.

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities - Dean McCullough, Jason Mohammad, Guy Mowbray, Snoochie Shy and Kate Thornton - race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome the remaining couples back to the Strictly ballroom, and with the quarter-finals and semi-finals on the horizon, everyone is determined to give their best. The Instant Dance challenge returns, in which the couples are tasked with improvising a routine in a style they have previously performed. With just minutes to hear their music, select and change into their outfits and hit the dance floor, who will rise to the challenge and secure the highest additional score on offer from the judges? Once all our couples have danced twice and the vote opens, who will get your support?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Karen Carney, Sophie Ellis-Bextor, Harry Hill, Judi Love, Niko Omilana, Tom Rosenthal and Ellie Simmonds.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: When an old friend returns, Martha faces the danger of exposure, forcing her to confess all to Kurt and make a risky decision to trust him. They must both keep Kamilla onside, even whilst keeping secrets from her and one another. Fuelled by both his complicated entanglements with Martha and Kurt and an effort to outmanoeuvre her, Friedrich makes a drastic move to catch Martha out.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights from four Premier League matches, including Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge of Manchester United against Brentford. Elsewhere, Leeds welcome Coventry to Elland Road, whilst Ipswich host Aston Villa. Plus highlights of Friday’s game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea.

programme.title: The Lady in the Van
programme.desc: 1970s Camden Town. Writer Alan Bennett's neighbours include the outspoken and unconventional Miss Shepherd, proudly residing in a van parked on the street. Offering space on his front drive for her vehicle begins a bizarre arrangement that he feels guilty about later exploiting in print. Acclaimed comedy drama from BBC Films based on actual events.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: In 2021, 19-year-old soldier Jaysley Beck was found dead in her army barracks. Through unprecedented access to her family, friends and former colleagues, Stacey Dooley traces her journey from excited young recruit to victim of sexual assault. As her family seeks answers and fights for change, the film explores the experiences of women in the armed forces and asks what more can be done to protect them.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.title: Jobfished
programme.desc: Catrin Nye investigates the glamorous design company that tricked its own staff into believing it was real through an online universe of fake profiles, stolen work and lies.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.desc: The Smith family embark upon a mammoth declutter. Stacey and the team challenge them to let go of half of their possessions, so that they can beautifully reorganise their life and home.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: A special episode of the historical sketch show about Queen Victoria, starring Sarah Hadland. We meet young Vicky as she becomes queen aged only 18, marries her true love, Albert, and has to put up with the open sewers at the not-so-luxurious Buckingham Palace. Meanwhile, across the world, we catch up with Australian outlaw Ned Kelly and discover plans for the Great Hedge of India. Yes, hedge! With, of course, our host Rattus to guide the way!

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: A special episode about King Alfred the Great, starring Tom Rosenthal. Watch Alfred argue with his older brothers then defeat the Vikings using his cunning hit-and-run tactics, summoning the spirit of Ed Sheeran. Meanwhile, across the world, Ant and Dec host a very special Chinese edition of I'm a Celebrity, and the Egyptians tell us how healthcare should really be done. With of, course, our host Rattus to guide the way!

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May test the Aston Martin Rapide, the Porsche Panamera Turbo and the Maserati Quattroporte as they attempt to find the world's greatest four-seat supercar. After an early morning start in the City of London, the boys embark on a road trip across the south of England, stop off for a race around a closed-off business park, and end up undertaking a rather special chauffeuring job. Meanwhile, Richard is on the test track in two very different muscle cars, the Chevrolet Camaro SS and Mercedes E63 AMG. And there's a double dose of celebrity as Harry Potter star Rupert Grint and F1 ace Rubens Barrichello take their turns as the Stars in a Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: On their first runs of the new season, Lisa is forced to stop when the unrelenting road knocks her engine apart, and Todd attempts an ambitious bush fix to muscle his load back onto the trailer. Meanwhile, rookie Scooter gets creative to squeeze his wide load down the narrow winter roads. Further west, Shaun checks ice thickness on his most important winter route - only to discover it's too thin to support his truck, forcing him to seek solutions with the crew building the ice road.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: Lisa’s truck loses all heat as temperatures plummet toward minus 40, forcing her to seek help from Scooter. When the two competitive drivers meet for the first time, they make a bet that changes the course of the season. On the road back to Muskie Creek, Todd suffers a catastrophic failure when the terrain rips the air lines from his trailer. Meanwhile, Shaun, Riley and Zach push further north on more aggressive routes to replace the business lost due to deadly thin ice on their regular run.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: Todd returns to face an old nemesis that once defeated him and destroyed his truck: Asheweig Road. Lisa tackles the longest run of the season so far, but disaster strikes when a fire breaks out beneath her truck - while she hauls barrels of explosive oil. Scooter is knocked backwards down an icy hill as he ventures into the unknown on a little-used goat trail. Further north, Shaun leads sons Riley and Zach over one of the continent's largest lakes on their first crossing of the massive frozen expanse.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: Todd hauls a massive machine as he fights his way home in a final showdown with his nemesis, the infamous Asheweig Road. After a risky brake fix during Lisa's longest run of her season, she searches for some home time to recharge. Scooter calls in a local road crew after losing a battle with an angry hill on his return trip along the goat trail. And Riley and Zach face a dangerous breakdown and a massive lake crossing on their first solo run without Shaun.

programme.title: Strike
programme.desc: Edie Ledwell, the co-creator of cult TV cartoon The Ink Black Heart, is being harassed by an online figure, Anomie. She asks Robin to uncover Anomie’s true identity.

programme.title: Strike
programme.desc: Robin, Strike and Barclay all take risks to further the investigation now that they think Anomie probably killed Edie Ledwell. Strike receives an unexpected and unwelcome visitor.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, James May and the Stig return. Jeremy asks why there aren't more three-wheeled cars in the world and investigates further with a closer look at the 1980s comedians' favourite, the Reliant Robin. Meanwhile, James gives Top Gear's favourite warhorse, the Toyota Hilux pickup, one final assignment as he attempts to drive one up an active volcano in Iceland and the Stig rips up the track in the new Bentley Continental Supersports. Richard gives the old Chevrolet Lacetti a dignified send-off before he and Clarkson host a star-studded tea party to welcome in a shiny new Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May attempt to find a trio of cars which are equally at home on the racetrack as they are transporting a family to the shops, for a budget of £5,000. They end up with a BMW M3, a Mercedes 190E and a Ford Sierra Cosworth, which they put through their paces in Europe's home of speed, Germany. James also makes a rare visit to the Top Gear track to test a pair of Porsches - the 911 Sport Classic and Boxster Spyder - and Alastair Campbell is the star in the all-new reasonably priced car.

programme.desc: Jobless is a sitcom all about the Adenugas, a middle-class British Nigerian family in Milton Keynes, in particular 16-year-old twin brother and sister Kehinde and Taiwo. Kenny is the family joker, who dreams of fame and fortune; sister Tai is, by contrast, sarcastic, super-smart and anxious to prove it. The twins live at home with their parents. Their mum, Bunmi, (chatty, energetic, control-freak tendencies, has a very stern side) runs Bunmi’s Beauty Salon, and despairs at her hapless offspring and their schemes to hit the big time. Tai and Kenny are desperate to make money by any means necessary – not only is financial independence very alluring, but the pressure they face from Bunmi doesn’t help. The twins’ different personalities inform their different approaches, however it seems neither of those personalities are quite compatible with the world of work.

programme.title: Nativity 2: Danger in the Manger!
programme.desc: An anxious teacher starts a new job at an under-achieving school and quickly finds himself struggling to cope with a wild classroom assistant, a group of under-performing kids and his own very pregnant wife. He soon becomes embroiled in a madcap plan to enter a national Song for Christmas competition and finds himself embarking on a disastrous road trip in search of the competition venue - the Christmas Castle. Lost in the wilderness with a class of small children, a baby and a donkey, he has to stand up, face his fears and try to lead them not only to safety, but victory.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: A podcaster is murdered whilst investigating the disappearance of a child. It’s a case that’s haunted Selwyn for many years, and now Neville and the team must lay its ghost to rest.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has had enough hassle with Christmas trees to last a lifetime, so this year she refuses to have one. But with Grandad's health a worry for everyone, is there something else missing this Christmas apart from just the tree?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It's the festive season once again in the Brown household, and Father Damian has organised a Christmas decoration contest. Agnes is keen to enter, especially as it might mean getting one over her old nemesis Hillary Nicholson. But she is soon distracted when Dermot and Buster give Agnes a 'Wi-Fi assistant', and she has trouble figuring out what to do with it. Meanwhile, Cathy is up for a promotion at work, and Dino and Rory give Buster a full makeover so he can look his best for an internet date. It's bound to go well - as long as she looks like she does in her photo.

programme.title: Man Up
programme.desc: Nancy, 34 years old and single, is travelling across London to toast another ten years of her parents' magical marriage. She runs into 40-year-old divorcee Jack, who mistakes her for his blind date. Nancy decides to go with it and starts the most chaotic journey of her life. A romantic comedy about taking chances, making decisions and rolling with the consequences.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom set in Manchester, starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Nicki decides on a pregnancy test, Moz is upset by the return of the severed hand, and Craig gets to bond with the volatile Cartoon Head.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series starring Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. All Moz has on his mind is the dead body he needs to get rid of. Meanwhile, Nicki has some important news to impart.

Meanwhile, Cartoon Head has lined up a special surprise for Derrick's stag party.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series with Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Moz wakes up next to someone shocking, discovers two hundred pairs of trainers in his living room, fills his kitchen with foam, and finds out that his landlord is on the way round.

programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series with Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Is Moz falling for his new neighbour, Judith? Is he being haunted by the ghost of Craig? And, more importantly, where can he hide the PC's crop of marijuana plants?

programme.desc: Manchester-based comedy series with Johnny Vegas as small-time dope dealer Moz. Moz makes a startling discovery about his new love. Scary OAP Mrs Coneybear arrives to perform a seance, and a plainclothes cop becomes trapped in the loft.

programme.desc: When disaster hits the Titanic, the Doctor uncovers a threat to the whole human race. Battling alongside aliens, saboteurs, robot Angels and a new friend called Astrid, can he stop the Christmas inferno?

programme.title: A Christmas Carol Goes Wrong
programme.desc: The Olivier Award-winning Mischief Theatre Company return to the small screen with their take on Dickens's famous festive fable. Blacklisted by the BBC after ruining Peter Pan, the Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society do not take their ban lying down and force themselves back on the BBC by hijacking the jewel of the Christmas schedule, a live production of A Christmas Carol, staged by a professional cast. As the Cornley gang try to make the show work on television, they soon realise they are completely out of their depth, with no idea how to direct a live studio or handle the special effects. Worse still, their internal rivalries are revealed on television, while an angry professional cast tries to get back into the studio.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: We find Miranda where we left her, with two proposals - one from Gary and one from Mike. Will she choose one of them or will she run away from the pressures of relationships and the fear of not coping with being a wife?

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: It's the final chance for Miranda to try to learn to accept herself and find contentment. Will it be alone, or does she find her one true love? One last chance to hang out with Miranda, Stevie, Penny, Tilly and Gary.

programme.title: Gavin & Stacey
programme.desc: Stacey's brother Jason arrives home early, much to Uncle Bryn's horror. Stacey has her hen night, and Gavin has two stag nights, the second of which reveals something about Stacey that could jeopardise the whole wedding.

programme.title: Gavin & Stacey
programme.desc: Comedy series based around the long-distance relationship of Essex boy Gavin and Welsh girl Stacey. The wedding day has finally arrived, but will they go through with it? Will Uncle Bryn finally admit to what happened on the fishing trip and will Nessa do what she knows she must?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Mobeen and Nate are just weeks from the end of their sentence, but Mobeen’s work as one of the prison’s 'listeners' gets him into trouble with a terrifying inmate from another wing - a man known simply as Megalodon. Megalodon is determined to get a transfer to Mobeen’s wing so he can confront him about meddling in his business. Mobeen and Nate also have to deal with prison officer Saj, who is a constant thorn in their side. Alongside all this, Mobeen gets a visit from Aqsa, who is getting frustrated with certain aspects of life at medical school. Mobeen also pays a visit to the prison’s multifaith chaplain, who is a familiar figure, and another old face has a mission for Mobeen that could throw him back into a whole world of trouble - but will he take it on?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Mobeen has landed himself in the prison infirmary, where he also has a mission – to befriend a man known as 'Memory Stick' and convince him to hand over vital information. In the infirmary, he also encounters a doctor, Nida, and there’s an instant spark between her and Mobeen. Nida also suggests she can help Aqsa with a placement for her medical degree, which she is thrilled with. Aqsa also receives some characteristically unhelpful advice from prison chaplain Uncle Shady. While Mobeen is in the hospital, Nate and Officer Harper develop a bromance that makes Mobeen jealous. Meanwhile, Megalodon is still trying to get transferred to Mobeen’s wing...

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: After weeks of travelling, filming and constant attention, life on the road is taking its toll on Bill. With brothers Joel and Johnny along for the ride, family offers an escape from fame. The Murrays reflect on losing their father young, and how caddying and golf bound nine siblings together. By the time they reach Cruit Island in Donegal, family reflection gives way to golfing rivalry.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in idyllic Bannau Brycheiniog with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk continues her epic journey deep, deep into film. She interrogates some of the world’s foremost filmmakers and critics, discovers an age of screen icons, from Marilyn Monroe to Wayne John, learns how Hollywood movies changed as American social values relaxed, and discovers how, believe it or not, other countries were making films as well. Along the way, she gives her verdict on classics like Jaws, Taxi Driver, and Citizen Ken - very much the Citizen Kane of films about people called Ken.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Paris is home to more award-winning pastry chefs than anywhere else in the world. Here, the day revolves around patisserie. Morning begins with the buttery flakes of a croissant. At midday, a baguette tucked under the arm signals lunch. And by the afternoon, mouthwatering sweet treats are savoured like miniature works of art. Resistance is futile, and Eva is seduced by the Paris-Brest, a rum baba, the macaron, a mango cake and dahlia, to name just a few.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Philippa, Nathan, Pete, Natalie and Sandra - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates the rewards of winter gardening - sharing ideas, inspiration and timely jobs to keep gardeners busy now, while reminding us that warmer days lie ahead. At Longmeadow, he has hellebores to plant, peas to sow and practical advice on propagating roses. Sue Kent gets to work on her allotment, where there’s always plenty to do during the colder months, including some clever composting. Jamie Butterworth takes a tour of one of Somerset’s most imaginative topiary gardens. In Belfast, a local community tells the tale of how their once neglected alleyway has become their pride and joy. Carol Klein unearths some radical new thinking on how flowers may be adapting to climate change, while Rekha Mistry travels to RHS Garden Bridgewater to see how garden varieties of tomato and mint are put to the test.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. This time, it's four members of the same family, Sarah, Paul, Curtis and Jessica. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Colin Murray and Edith Bowman discover tips and treats at the food and music festival in Newcastle. They find out how to create award-winning burgers and reveal the secrets of chips, French-Canadian style. Briony May Williams goes on the trail of the nation’s favourite herb, and chef Julie Lin sets sail to find Scotland’s most valuable fish. Farmer Meinir Howells investigates the growing popularity of keeping chickens.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael travels from Alnmouth to Bamburgh Castle, an icon of Northumberland. Along the way, he takes to the waves in a traditional skiff and discover a fascinating map which charts shipwrecks.

programme.title: Liz Bonnin's Wild Caribbean
programme.desc: The volcanic islands of the Lesser Antilles, built by eruptions and shaped by the ocean surrounding them, are some of the most biodiverse landscapes of the Caribbean, where humans have developed a special relationship with their wild surroundings. On Mayreau, Liz joins a team of residents repairing their vibrant coral, which has been damaged by disease. On neighbouring Union Island, she goes on patrol with a local environmental army to help protect the Union Island gecko, one of the smallest reptiles in the world. In St Vincent, Liz hikes one of the most active volcanoes in the region – La Soufriere – to find the brightly coloured St Vincent parrot. And in her ancestral home of Trinidad, she relives one of her most magnificent wildlife encounters: the flight of the scarlet ibis.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team travel to Londonderry for the first time in the show's history. Amongst the items under scrutiny are some very intricately produced hand-cut pictures, a cache of silver valued at over £100,000 and a cushion woven from human hair.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Ickworth House, a Georgian mansion in Suffolk built for the Earls of Bristol. Paul Martin is joined by experts Will Axon and Philip Serrell. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at a local auction. Will casts an appreciative eye over a piece of Martinware but will a miniature long case clock bought at the car boot for £1 prove to be the star find? Paul also heads to the Suffolk coast to explore the magical House in the Clouds in Thorpeness, a fantasy holiday village built in the early years of the 20th century.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Catherine Bohart, Chesney Hawkes, Rebecca Keatley and Jason Mohammad take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games skateboard?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more gossip and behind-the-scenes news from the world of Strictly. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill has an exclusive look at what the couples are wearing at the weekend.

programme.desc: Wanting a new start in Devon, a couple with a budget of £650,000 enlist Jules Hudson’s house-hunting knowhow to find a detached family home with a large garden for their two young children and some income potential. Whilst in the county, Jules gets stuck into some woodcraft using nothing but steam to sculpt some impressive interior design pieces.

programme.title: Monty Don’s British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the south west of the country to visit some of Britain’s most exotic gardens, thanks to the warm and wet climate. On this journey, Monty also goes to some of the country's most historic gardens, as well as some challenging contemporary ones.

programme.title: Why...?
programme.desc: On 24 September 2025, the main road outside one of Bangkok's major hospitals collapsed. The giant sinkhole, the size of two tennis courts, snapped water pipes, ripped down power lines, and swallowed two vehicles. During the day, it continued to grow, threatening the foundations of the hospital and forcing close to a thousand staff and patients to evacuate the building. Ampan Vimonvattana, vice dean of Vajira Hospital, witnessed the collapse: 'The earth swallowed everything... it pulled the road surface, the soil, anything on top. Even the electrical poles got dragged down. It was really scary.' Why Sinkholes Collapse explores cases of sinkholes in Godstone, Surrey, a collapse under a main road in Yashio City in Japan and the underground quarries that are beneath ten per cent of Paris to help explain why sinkholes occur and how they can be prevented.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk heads to Hollywood, Los Angeles, for the final part of her staggeringly comprehensive history of cinema, where she accosts some of the people behind the biggest movies of recent years, from The Avengers to Transformers to the Flintstones film. She takes a look at Star Wars, Jurassic Park, Toy Story, the home video revolution, the rise of the blockbuster franchise and the state of cinema today. And with the rise of artificial intelligence, she asks the question: is Hollywood finished... or just about to be finished?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Cabaret
programme.desc: Bob Fosse's award-winning musical, set in 1930s Berlin. A love affair develops between cabaret singer Sally Bowles and a naive young Englishman amid the city's decadent cafe society, during the gradual rise of German fascism.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The four chefs who have survived the intensity of the heats are back in the kitchen. Now they must prove that they have the skills to take on the next level of the competition.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports?

programme.desc: Entrepreneur Aoibheann has found the ideal location to retreat from her busy life in Galway - a modest derelict cottage in the heart of the Burren. But Aoibheann’s creativity and plans for the cottage know no bounds, and if she can't rein in some of her ideas, will this renovation ever progress?

Pike are wily fish, always hiding in the dark reeds and waiting to ambush their prey. Bob has a fail-safe method to try, but will the duo be able to outwit the elusive creatures?

programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Plantswoman Carol Klein shares with us a year in her garden at Glebe Cottage in north Devon. Carol has looked after her garden for over 30 years, each with its own rewards and delights, as well as problems and challenges. Follow Carol as her garden grows, flourishes, dies and is reborn. The first episode covers January and February. The frosts have not yet released their grip on the garden, and the devastation of a hard winter is scattered all around. There is much to do - cutting back, preparing the soil and planting garlic. The first green shoots of the year begin to appear as drifts of snowdrops carpet the woodland floor and hellebores reveal their ravishing colours. A local woodsman joins Carol to lay a native hedge. Slowly, the first signs of spring appear.

Other highlights include their 2011 set at Glastonbury - which featured classic tracks such as Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where the Streets Have No Name and Pride (In the Name of Love) - and a 2009 performance of Vertigo that wasn't just at the BBC, but on it, with the band singing from the roof of Broadcasting House.

programme.title: Cashback

programme.title: The Good Heart
